name: SideNav
intent: The app's main navigation: a brand rail of sections on the left, each with an optional second-level menu that flies out beside it.
usage: Put one SideNav on the left of the app shell, under the AppHeader, full height. It is one component: items are the rail sections (icon and label), endItems sit at the bottom of the rail, and a section's children make its second-level menu. Hovering a section rolls its menu out beside the rail; moving off the nav or picking a link rolls it back in. Clicking a section opens its first link, so a section with no menu still works. pin docks the menu open beside the rail; the × closes it. expanded shows the labels (the AppHeader menu button toggles it). A long menu is kept on screen and scrolls with overflow rows at the top and bottom. See contracts/sidenav.json for the full contract. In a box narrower than 640px, the kit's mobile break, there is no room for a rail beside the page, so the nav is a drawer: it takes its open width with the labels shown whether or not expanded is passed, and it leaves the sliding to the frame around it.

items.itemShape: { id: string; label: string; icon: string; href?: string; children?: SideNavChild[] } | { divider: true }
items.note: Rail sections, top to bottom. icon is a Material Symbols name. children is the second-level menu: { id, label, href? } links and { divider: true } lines.

endItems.note: Sections pinned to the bottom of the rail, like Recycle Bin and Processes. Same shape as items.

current.note: Controlled id of the current page: a section or a link in its menu. Marks the link and its section.

defaultCurrent.note: Starting page when current is not controlled; SideNav then moves it on each click.

onNavigate.note: (id: string) => void. A section click passes its first link's id (or its own id when it has no menu).

expanded.note: Rail shows labels, 170px wide. Off, it is a 56px icon rail. Wire it to the AppHeader navOpen.

pinned.note: Controlled pin. The menu docks beside the rail, full height, with a border and no shadow, and pushes the page over.

defaultPinned.note: Starting pin when pinned is not controlled. The docked menu is the current section's, or the first section with a menu until one is opened.

onPinnedChange.note: (pinned: boolean) => void. Called by the pin and × buttons in the menu header.

useWhen: The main navigation of the app shell, on every page.
Sections with their own pages under them: the rail picks the section, the menu picks the page.
doNot: Do not invent a Sidebar, NavRail, Flyout or local menu beside it.
Do not put page actions, filters or tabs in it. Those belong in the page.
Do not nest a third level. A section has one menu of links, split by dividers.
Do not use DropdownMenu or Tabs for app navigation.
a11y: A nav landmark named by label. Sections and links are real links (or buttons without href) you Tab through.
Enter on a section opens its page. The chevron after a section with a menu is its cascade button: Enter opens the menu and moves focus into it, with aria-expanded.
Tab moves through the menu links. Escape leaves the menu back to its cascade button; Escape in the rail closes an open menu.
The current page has aria-current=page. On touch, a tap on a section with a menu opens the menu.
Collapsed rail icons show their label in a kit Tooltip. The roll animation turns off with reduced motion.
snippet:
<SideNav
  items={sections}
  endItems={[{ id: "recycle", label: "Recycle Bin", icon: "recycling" }]}
  current={pageId}
  onNavigate={openPage}
  expanded={navOpen}
/>

examples.title: Rail
examples.usage: The closed rail: icons only. Hover Revenue or Settings for their menu; click a section to open its first page.

examples.title: Expanded
examples.usage: expanded shows the labels. The chevron marks a section with a menu.

examples.title: Pinned
examples.usage: The menu docked open beside the rail, with a border and no shadow. × closes it. Here General Ledger is the current page, so Revenue and its link show selected.
